long_biography.plain_text:
A 1978 swimming-pool accident left Johnson nearly paralysed and changed the scale of his ambitions. He moved away from a goal of mass homebuilding toward one-off developments designed around difficult land. Through Victor International, he went on to create dozens of residential and commercial communities, notably turning a former cement-plant site on Lake Michigan into the award-winning Bay Harbor resort community.

Years of sailing through the Caribbean led Johnson to the site that became Oil Nut Bay on Virgin Gorda. The 400-acre community combines villas, resort facilities and marina infrastructure with low-density planning, underground utilities, renewable energy and conservation areas. He remains founder and chairman of Victor International and developer-resident of Oil Nut Bay, extending a career centred on luxury real estate and land-sensitive community design.
